'''Suitengu''' (水天宮) is a Shinto shrine located in {{ill|Hokkaido|en|Hokkaido|qid=Q35581|lt=Hokkaido}} {{ill|Otaru|en|Otaru|qid=Q242108|lt=Otaru City}}. Its former status was that of a {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|WD=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Local Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}.

It is sited at a location offering a panoramic view of {{ill|Port of Otaru|ja|小樽港|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otaru Port|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q10959354}}, and is renowned as one of the famous spots for {{ill|Cherry blossom|en|Cherry blossom|qid=Q871991|lt=Cherry Blossoms}} in Otaru City. The steep stairs and slopes descending toward the seaside area of {{ill|Q11428313|ja|堺町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sakaimachi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11428313}} are known as Gaijin-zaka<ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.city.otaru.lg.jp/simin/koho/sakamati/1402.html |title=コッフさんと外人坂 前編 |work=おたる坂まち散歩 |publisher={{ill|Otaru|en|Otaru|qid=Q242108|lt=Otaru City}} |accessdate=2016-05-24}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.city.otaru.lg.jp/simin/koho/sakamati/1403.html |title=コッフさんと外人坂 後編 |work=おたる坂まち散歩 |publisher=小樽市 |accessdate=2016-05-24}}</ref>. A straight road connects the shrine to {{ill|Otaru Park|ja|小樽公園|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otaru Park|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q24316228}}, located on the hillside, thereby integrating the surrounding landscape<ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.jila-hokkaido.com/gyouji_/kitanozouensisan/kitanozoen_all/4_otaru/Isan-4(Otaru).pdf |title=小樽公園 |format=PDF |publisher={{ill|Landscape architecture|ja|日本造園学会|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japan Landscape Architecture Society|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 造園|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q47844}} Hokkaido Branch |accessdate=2016-05-12}}</ref>. Within the precincts, there stand monuments such as the {{ill|Takuboku Ishikawa|en|Takuboku Ishikawa|qid=Q467747|lt=Ishikawa Takuboku}} poetry monument, the Mitsuya Yōson (みつやようそん) haiku monument, and the {{ill|Bun'ichirō Kawamura|ja|河邨文一郎|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawasomura Bun'ichirō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11554131}} poetry monument<ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=http://otaru-journal.com/2005/10/post-837.php |title=水天宮の啄木歌碑を移設！新たな装いでお目見え！ |date=2005-10-15 |work={{ill|Q11462138|ja|小樽ジャーナル|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otaru Journal|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11462138}} |publisher=小樽ジャーナル社 |accessdate=2016-05-24}}</ref>.

== Enshrined Deities ==
The shrines sharing the same name as the Suitengu of {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|en|Fukuoka Prefecture|qid=Q123258|lt=Fukuoka Prefecture}} {{ill|Kurume|en|Kurume|qid=Q320934|lt=Kurume City}}, designated as the head shrine, enshrine figures including {{ill|Emperor Antoku|en|Emperor Antoku|qid=Q316651|lt=Emperor Antoku}}, whereas the deities enshrined here are different and do not belong to that lineage{{Sfn|小野|1999|p=103}}.
* {{ill|Mizuhanome|en|Mizuhanome|qid=Q8191796|lt=Yatsunahome deity}} (Mizuhanome-no-Kami)
* {{ill|Ukemochi|en|Ukemochi|qid=Q2280323|lt=Ukemochi}} (Ukemochi-no-Kami)
* {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊邪那岐神|lt=Izanagi-no-Kami|lt_ja=伊邪那岐神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi|qid=Q813858}} (Izanagi-no-Kami)
* {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊邪那美神|lt=Izanami-no-Kami|lt_ja=伊邪那美神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanami|qid=Q682306|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q682306}} (Izanami-no-Kami)

== History ==
* {{ill|1859|en|1859|qid=Q7687|lt=1859}} ({{ill|Ansei|en|Ansei|qid=Q1327259|lt=Ansei}} 6), established.
* {{ill|1900|en|1900|qid=Q2034|lt=1900}} ({{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era}} 33), upon a petition by the residents, the Ukemochi from the neglected {{ill|Inari shrine|en|Inari shrine|qid=Q514480|lt=Inari Shrine}} was enshrined alongside.
* {{ill|1919|en|1919|qid=Q2157|lt=1919}} ({{ill|Taishō era|en|Taishō era|qid=Q329174|lt=Taishō}} 8), driven by the sentiments of natives from Shiga Prefecture, the shrine building was reconstructed and the two deities known as Nakuin Nison ({{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊邪那岐神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi|qid=Q813858}} and {{ill|Izanami|ja|伊邪那美神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanami|qid=Q682306|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q682306}}) from {{ill|Taga shrine|ja|多賀神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taga Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11431089}} were additionally enshrined.
* {{ill|1923|en|1923|qid=Q2169|lt=1923}} (Taishō 12), it was elevated to a village shrine and designated as a {{ill|Shinsen Heihaku-ryō Kyōshinjinja|ja|神饌幣|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}*
